messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a cross-quant bake comparing GPTQ vs AWQ on `redwood-chat-7b` with INT8/FP8 variants. Observation: when prefix KV cache is ON + continuous batching enabled, p99 latency spikes and occasional accuracy jitter on long-prefix prompts. details below.

alex: numbers pls. latency + accuracy deltas?

maria: TL;DR: AWQ-int8 gives ~0.8% EM loss vs fp16 on our eval set, GPTQ-int8 ~0.5%. With prefix cache disabled, p99=180ms. With prefix cache enabled + cont-batching window=25ms, p99 jumps to 420-680ms on bursty traffic. Accuracy delta becomes noisier on >1k token prefixes.

jun: hmm. is this cache miss storming or kv-corruption?

maria: not corruption. traces show frequent KV eviction/repop cycles. hypothesis: continuous batching groups requests with overlapping prefixes; cache lookup latencies + queuing delay cause some requests to wait for cache warmups, then later batches populate cache and following requests get different KV hits mid-request -> sequence-length/attention alignment differences that change decoder internal states slightly, leading to nondeterministic token choices in the tail.

sree: can you paste the batcher + kvcache config you used?

maria: sure:
```
batcher:
  enable_continuous_batching: true
  window_ms: 25
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_size: 16
kvcache:
  prefix_cache_enabled: true
  cache_shards: 8
  ttl_ms: 600000
  eviction_policy: lru
```

maria: also ran a run with `continuous_batching: false` and identical traffic shape — p99 stayed low and accuracy was stable.

alex: interesting. any difference between AWQ vs GPTQ beyond accuracy? like memory layout impacting cache lookup speed?

maria: yes. AWQ's kernel path seems to have slightly higher per-token decode overhead on our GPU (profiling shows +6-10us/token in the inner loop). That amplifies queuing when batcher waits to fill/window, so more overlap across requests hitting cache cold spots. GPTQ path is a tad faster, so fewer interleavings.

jun: did you try bumping window_ms down to 10ms or increase max_batch_size?

maria: tried 10ms -> reduces p99 but increases overall token cost (less efficient batching). Increasing max_batch_size to 32 increased tail latency (bigger batches sometimes mean one straggler stalls everyone).

sree: any error logs? deploy-bot + ci-bot traces?

ci-bot: test-run-2100001234 completed. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/runs/2100001234. contains perf traces and sample diffs.

maria: sample diffs show marginal token divergence concentrated after long prefixes (>800 tokens) and for generation tasks with frequent stop tokens. Example diff excerpt:
```
ref: "...and the final recommendation was to deprecate the old api."
new: "...and the final recommendation was to deprecate the legacy api."
```
semantically same but different tokenization path.

alex: action items?

maria: proposal:
- short term: disable prefix_cache for redwood-chat-7b on AWQ-int8 in hosted canary (rollback if regression)
- mid term: instrument per-request cache-hit timelines and KV lifecycle spans (start/end) in console traces
- experiments: run controlled sim with synthetic workload to isolate overlap windows (vary window_ms, kernel latency, prefix similarity)
- long term: add deterministic fallback for KV lookups during continuous batching (serve from transient snapshot until batch completes)

jun: +1 on instrumentation. also add an eval harness that measures token-level nondet rate vs prefix-length.

sree: I'll pick up the canary and the tracing changes. assigning to me.

maria: thanks. I'll queue the synthetic sims and add the detailed perf traces to the CI artifacts. linking dashboard for folks: https://dash.redwood/perf/2100001234

alex: nice detective work. keep notes short in the PR so SRE can triage quickly. :thumbsup:

maria: will do.

deploy-bot: deploy request submitted for "disable-prefix-cache" on canary/redwood-chat-7b (AWQ-int8). request id: dply-2100001234.

sree: monitoring alerts wired. will report back after 30m canary window.

maria: leaving logs and sample diffs in the run artifact. ping me if you want pair debugging.

jun: bookmarking the sim configs. thanks team.
